searchText: Hi Guys, Abhishek this side Have one doubt What is the reason of limiting stake of validator to 32 ETH ? No more No less No more: a very large staking capital in one validator could take control of a committee. No less: a very small staking capital would make it cheaper to attack the network. > No less: a very small staking capital would make it cheaper to attack the network. How so? Wouldn't you still need 51%, 67% or whatever of the total staked amount to attack the network? IIUIC, the reason not to lower it has to do with limiting the work needed for signature aggregation. Yeah by attack I meant the cost of verification. Probably bad choice of words. The original rationale for those numbers I think comes from https://medium.com/@VitalikButerin/parametrizing-casper-the-decentralization-finality-time-overhead-tradeoff-3f2011672735 There is also an elaboration in the Serenity design rationale doc, https://notes.ethereum.org/@vbuterin/rkhCgQteN?type=view#Why-32-ETH-validator-sizes, which refers to the post mentioned above Thanks Guys Will go through docs :thumbsup: How does it solve multiple identities ? Like if I stake 320 Or I stake 32 with 10 diff accounts Above 32 eth, stake is not effective. The balance is there, but it doesn't count towards voting. So you have to split it between validators to increase effect on the network, and earn rewards with it. If you have many validators and they happen to be included in the same committee you may take control But if you only have one, then every time you are in control of the committee right, the protocol requires stake to be divided into multiple validators, to make the random shuffling of validators between committees more effective okay got it thanks

No less: a very small staking capital would make it cheaper to attack the network.
